responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the PA-RISC (HPPA) architecture, covering the core machine description, ABI rules, register models, and operating-system object-format variants needed to lower GCC RTL into PA-specific code and assembly. Its central files define the PA instruction patterns, predicates, constraints, target macros, machine modes, and option set (`pa.md`, `predicates.md`, `constraints.md`, `pa.h`, `pa-modes.def`, `pa.opt`), while the main implementation (`pa.cc`/`pa.c`) supplies the target hooks for addressing, reload and legality checks, calling conventions, frame layout, prologue/epilogue generation, scheduling and costs, symbol and section handling, builtins, and final asm output. The module also contains the PA32 and PA64 register/ABI splits, 64-bit startup assumptions, and substantial OS-specific configuration layers for SOM and ELF targets across HP-UX, Linux, NetBSD, and OpenBSD, including release-specific HP-UX driver/spec logic and linker/runtime conventions. Together these files make this module responsible for all PA-RISC-specific code generation behavior, assembler syntax, object-format integration, and target-option policy, distinguishing it from generic GCC middle-end code and from backends for other architectures.
